result.summary: Re-gate of Step 2b limited to the Step 2c rework fix (commit 15b6ec2, handoffs/WF02-REQ-018/step-02-backend-dev-rework1.json), not a full re-review of the whole requirement (already PASSed at handoffs/WF02-REQ-018/step-02b-reviewer.json). Read git show 15b6ec2 in full myself: it touches exactly apps/bot/src/domain/auditLog.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.test.ts, and its own handoff bookkeeping -- confirmed against git diff master...HEAD --name-only, no apps/web files, no unrelated changes, handlers/checkin.ts itself is untouched (the fix lives entirely in the domain layer, one composed entry point covers every caller). S5 gap closure verified LIVE, not by reading code: stood up a fresh scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432), ran `npx drizzle-kit migrate`, built the bot (`npm run build`), and wrote a throwaway script (apps/bot/verify_regate_audit.mjs, deleted after use, confirmed via git status clean) that constructs a real grammY Bot wired to the compiled makeCheckInHandler(db) with a stubbed sendMessage transformer, seeds a real chapter/venue/two events (one future, one already-ended)/one registered member user, and dispatches real bot.handleUpdate() calls with correctly-formed bot_command entities (grammY's command() filter requires an entity, not just leading '/' text -- my first script pass produced 0 dispatches for exactly this reason, caught and fixed before trusting any result). Counted audit_log rows before/after each of all THREE refusal branches myself: - no-user (unregistered tg_id): before=0, after=1, delta=+1. Row: {actor_user_id: null, action: 'checkin.refused', entity: 'event', entity_id: , payload: {reason: 'no-user'}}. - not-staff-for-event (registered member, no event_staff row for the target event): before=1, after=2, delta=+1. Row: {actor_user_id: , action: 'checkin.refused', entity: 'event', entity_id: , payload: {reason: 'not-staff-for-event'}}. - event-ended (same member IS staffed on a second event whose ends_at is in the past): before=2, after=3, delta=+1. Row: {actor_user_id: , action: 'checkin.refused', entity: 'event', entity_id: , payload: {reason: 'event-ended'}}. All three: exactly +1 (never 0, never 2+), correct reason string, actor_user_id correctly null only for no-user and the resolved internal users.id (never tg_id) for the other two. This is a stronger re-derivation than BACKEND-DEV's own rework handoff, which live-tested only 2 of 3 branches and reasoned the third was 'redundant' given unit coverage -- I do not accept a producer's own scope-narrowing of what the reviewer verifies, so I ran all three myself. docker compose torn down (`docker compose down -v`) and the scratch script deleted after use; git status confirmed clean before committing. ActorUserId widening (auditLog.ts: `string` -> `string | null`): confirmed the schema already permits it (db/schema.ts line 314, actor_user_id has no .notNull() -- comment: 'a genuinely system-initiated action ... has no human actor'). Grepped every other writeAuditLog call site (domain/event.ts x4, domain/eventStaff.ts x2, domain/venue.ts x3) -- every one passes a plain `actorUserId` variable sourced from an already-authenticated/resolved user, i.e. a non-null string; widening the parameter type to include null is backward compatible (TS allows passing a narrower `string` where `string | null` is expected) and `npm run build` confirms zero type errors across the whole diff -- no other caller's contract broke. PII check (S11-adjacent, my own independent read, not deferred to SECURITY-REVIEWER): buildCheckinRefusalAudit's payload carries exactly one key, `reason`, one of three fixed enum literals ('no-user' | 'not-staff-for-event' | 'event-ended') -- never free text, never a Telegram username, never tg_id. entityId is the event's internal uuid, matching checkin.ts's own pre-existing 'not-found before authorization' precedent that event ids are not secret. Confirmed live in the query output above: no phone/email/username-shaped values appear anywhere in the three rows produced. 'No audit row on success' judgment call: I agree with BACKEND-DEV's reasoning and do not treat it as a gap. S5's own text names the refusal case specifically ('the one case where the log matters most is an attempted unauthorized scan') and the /checkin stub performs no check-in write of its own on the ok=true branch (design section 0.3, unchanged) -- there is no state change or disclosure yet to log, and REQ-028/029 is the correct place to add a success-path audit row once an actual check-in write exists. Logging success here now would be inventing a business rule neither S5 nor the design asks for. No MINOR note needed -- this is a reasoned agreement, not a nudge away from a documented decision. Test count and commands re-run myself, real output: `npm run lint` (0 errors, the pre-existing 2 apps/web warnings are unrelated to this diff, unchanged from the prior PASS), `npm run build` (both workspaces, tsc clean), `npx vitest run` -- 10 files / 118 tests passed (up from 114 at the prior PASS, the 4 new buildCheckinRefusalAudit cases in eventStaffAuthorization.test.ts: 'no-user' actorUserId null, 'not-staff-for-event' and 'event-ended' actorUserId = resolved user.id never tg_id, and a dedicated PII/shape-lockdown case asserting the payload has exactly one key). Read all 4 new test cases -- they lock down every branch this fix claims to cover, no gap. Design-system check: N/A, no visual/CSS surface in this bot-only domain-layer change. No anti-pattern from docs/agents/anti-patterns.md applies. No docs/agents/decisions/ record is contradicted -- decisions/0004 (domain logic outside handlers) is honored, decisions/0006 (no now() in time-dependent predicates) is unaffected by this diff (evaluationTime is still the only clock input, unchanged from the prior PASS). No migration/schema file in this diff (auditLog.ts's type widening has no .sql companion, matching the security finding's own note that the column was already nullable) -- S13 sign-off duty not triggered.
